title: Audit forwarder: Idempotency keys, HMAC integrity, and SLO-tiered delivery
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Improve delivery guarantees, integrity, and observability for outbound audit integrations (webhooks, Splunk HEC, Datadog HTTP) while supporting differentiated SLO tiers. We need a practical architecture that prevents silent loss, enables efficient deduplication for downstream sinks, and fits into Redwood's Dedicated/Private deployment constraints.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: outbound forwarding pipeline (post-ingest) that ships tenant audit events to external SIEMs and HTTP sinks. Covers HMAC signing, idempotency tokens, disk-backed spooler, retry/backoff policies, DLQ semantics, and per-tenant SLO routing. Includes Splunk HEC special-casing (event batching, ack mapping), Datadog HTTP specifics, and generic webhook semantics.
- Non-goals: changing upstream audit schema, redesigning tenant auth, or adding new sink adapters beyond Splunk/Datadog/webhook. Exact-once across heterogeneous external systems is a best-effort feature (we will provide dedupe guarantees, not distributed transactions).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
1) Envelope + Idempotency: every outbound event is wrapped in an envelope with a globally unique event_id (UUIDv4) and a dedupe_token = sha256(tenant_id + event_id + forwarder_generation). Dedupes are stored as time-windowed tokens in Redis for 7 days. Trade-off: small Redis cost but enables at-least-once -> effectively once behavior for sinks that support idempotency.

2) Integrity: Attach an X-Redwood-Signature header using HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical envelope. Keys are customer-specific forwarding keys stored in KMS; rotated keys will be published with a key-id header. This protects downstream consumers and enables them to verify authenticity. Trade-off: KMS calls are required for key access; we cache signing keys for short TTL to limit latency.

3) Local spooler + durable queue: For transient downstream failures, use a disk-backed spool (leveldb-backed queue) per forwarder shard. This prevents memory overload and supports resuming across restarts (important for private deployments that may be preempted). Queue entries include retry_count, next_retry_at, and the envelope JSON. Trade-off: disk IO but much more robust under load.

4) SLO-tiered routing and policy: Customers are tagged with delivery tier (standard, premium, enterprise). Premium/enterprise use higher retry budgets, longer DLQ retention, and a parallel dedicated lane (separate thread pool) to avoid head-of-line blocking. Standard tier uses tighter retry windows to keep costs down. Trade-off: increased complexity in scheduling and allocation.

5) Delivery semantics and sink adapters: Default is at_least_once. For sinks that support idempotency (Splunk HEC with client-provided event IDs, some Datadog endpoints), we include dedupe_token and HMAC to enable de-duplication and practical exactly-once behavior. For webhooks, we expect idempotency support via consumer-provided 2XX semantics; we provide idempotency_token header and recommend 2XX/202 semantics.

6) Acks and mapping: For Splunk HEC we map HEC response codes and messages to internal ack states. 200/201 -> ack, 400 -> permanent fail -> DLQ, 429/503 -> transient -> retry with backoff and jitter. Webhook 2XX -> ack; 5XX/429 -> retry. Datadog 429 -> backoff per Retry-After header.

7) Ordering: We do not guarantee global ordering across tenants; we support optional per-stream sequence numbers when a tenant opts into ordered delivery. When enabled we use per-tenant sequence queues with stall detection and SLA bypass (enterprise tier can enforce ordering by reserving worker slots).

Observability and SLOs:
- Metrics: per-tenant forwarded_count, ack_latency_histogram, retry_rate, dlq_rate, hmac_failures, dedupe_hits.
- Traces: include envelope id as trace tag, and record forward attempts as spans.
- Dashboards: SLO heatmap for ack latency and percent of events delivered within 30s/5m. Alerts: DLQ rate > 0.1% of forwarded for 10m, retry_rate spike, spool disk usage > 75%.

Security considerations:
- HMAC key protection (KMS/HSM) and key rotation plan.
- Harden spool files on disk (fsync policy, permission hardening).
- Ensure tenant-scoped key access and RBAC checks before forwarding.
- Audit all forward attempts to internal audit index with forwarding result and final disposition.

Testing plan:
- Load test: 100k events/s simulated across 1k tenants with randomized sink failures.
- Fault injection: simulate TCP drops, 429 bursts, KMS unavailable, and disk full.
- End-to-end verification: deploy a test consumer that verifies HMAC and dedupe behavior.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag gated behind ff:forwarder_v2 for internal and staging tenants.
2) Canary: enable for <10 tenants on enterprise tier and run 48h smoke + load validation.
3) Gradual tenant ramp by percent and tiers.
4) Full account opt-in UI and migration runbook for customers who want upgraded guarantees.

Operational runbook (high level):
- On consumer 5XX spike: throttle retries, increase backoff window, notify SRE and customer.
- On spool disk pressure: pause standard-tier forwarding, promote retention policies, alert.
- On repeated HMAC mismatches: rotate signing keys and invalidate cache; contact receiving partner.

Backward compatibility: headers X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Dedupe-Token are optional; older forwarders will continue to send bare payloads. New consumers should validate signature when supplied.

Open questions:
- Deduplication retention window (7d default) — question on compliance retention overlap with customer retention policies.
- Exact TTL and eviction strategy for dedupe tokens in Redis when private deployments don't want Redis dependency (fallback to local LRU store).
- SLA pricing knobs for enterprise tenants for longer retry budgets.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Triage: Identified as P0 due to customer incidents where events were lost during short Splunk outages. Assigned to Diego.
2026-02-25 - Design review: Security team requested HMAC header format and KMS rotation plan. Agreed to include key-id header and caching with 5m TTL.
2026-03-02 - Implementation started: added leveldb-backed spool library prototype; benching write throughput.
2026-03-05 - Security review scheduled: SSO team to validate access controls for forwarding keys. Added 'security_review_required' flag.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/pull/482 - implements envelope, dedupe token, and HMAC signing. Tests added for Splunk HEC ack mapping.
2026-03-12 - Integration tests: simulated Datadog 429 Retry-After handling and verified exponential backoff with jitter. Next: canary rollout prep.
acceptance_criteria: Forwarder signs envelopes with HMAC and includes key-id header
Deduplication reduces duplicates to <0.01% under high-retry scenarios
Splunk HEC adapter maps acks correctly and honors 429 Retry-After
Disk-backed spool survives forwarder process restart without data loss
Feature flag allows per-tenant opt-in and rollback
